correctness.rationale: Exact inverse-state telescoping decomposes the signed error into negative reciprocal terminal tail plus positive Euler quadrature defects. Before the step cap, the inverse square-root variable decreases by epsilon/(2 sqrt(2k)) with relative O(sqrt epsilon), implying the sharp early-step count; each uncapped quadrature defect is epsilon squared/(2k) times 1+O(sqrt epsilon). The capped phase has O(epsilon^-1/2) steps and O(epsilon^3/2) aggregate defect; terminal overshoot changes reciprocal tail by O(epsilon^3/2). The result and work coefficient follow. Rational exact identity tests and finite numerical checks executed, but are not an infinite proof.
